inlines.v: A'LIENATE, verb transitive [Latin alieno.] 1. To transfer title, property or right to another; as, to alienate lands, or sovereignty. 2. To estrange; to withdraw, as the affections; to make indifferent or averse, where love or friendship before subsisted; with from; as, to alienate the heart or affections; to alienate a man from the friends of his youth. 3. To apply to a wrong use. They shall not alienate the first fruits of the land. Ezekiel 48:14. A'LIENATE, adjective [Latin alienatus.] Estranged; withdrawn from; stranger to; with from. O alienate from God, O spirit accurst. The whigs were alienate from truth.
